facts.fact: The Nzika Digital ID Wallet was launched in Lilongwe on 16 September 2026 by the National Registration Bureau with partners including UNDP, with more than 22,000 reportedly enrolled by launch, per the Maravi Post column.

Nzika is a digital identity wallet that lets citizens hold digital versions of their National ID and certain civil registration documents, which the column says could make it easier to prove who they are.
The column says World Bank-supported programmes include plans involving digital identity authentication, electronic signatures and electronic know-your-customer services.
facts.system: World Bank-supported digital identity authentication and e-signature plans

MWI.note: The wallet holds certain civil registration documents, but no exchange of records between civil register and ID system is stated.

facts.fact: Malawi's national identity system holds information on more than 13.5 million registered people, per current reporting cited by the column; against 22.2 million population that is about 61% (share computed from the held population).

MWI.note: No statement on a number given at birth.
Laxton supplies and maintains registration kits with remote software support, but the document does not say who operates or owns the ID system.
No public register keyed on the national ID number is stated.

facts.fact: Malawi's national identity system contains information on more than 13.5 million registered people, including names, photographs and fingerprints, per current reporting cited by the column.
